tldr: This is not one developing event: three unrelated arXiv papers share the word "adaptive" and one idea, spending scarce resources where they help most. LAND (Nov 2) varies Best-of-N draws per input, and ASP (Nov 6) schedules RL rollouts to cut idle GPU time.
whats_new: A Nov 9 theory paper shows adaptive quantization keeps TD learning's fast convergence rate even when an agent's updates cross a rate-limited channel.
why_it_matters: Each paper targets a different budget: inference samples (LAND), RL-training GPU utilization (ASP), and communication bandwidth (TD quantization); only the first two touch production LLM stacks today.

beats.headline: LAND learns how many Best-of-N draws each input deserves
beats.summary: Fixed-N sampling wastes compute on inputs whose candidate scores barely vary.

beats.headline: ASP schedules asynchronous RL rollouts to reduce underutilization
beats.summary: Targets padding bubbles and other idle time across multi-instance LLM RL rollouts.

beats.headline: Adaptive quantization preserves TD-learning rates over rate-limited links
beats.summary: Policy evaluation with linear function approximation under a bandwidth constraint.

open_questions: Does LAND publish compute savings against fixed-N Best-of-N on a standard reward-model benchmark?
Is ASP's scheduler released as code, or integrated into an open RL framework?
Does the adaptive-quantization result extend beyond linear function approximation?
take_for_builders: If you run Best-of-N or async RL, read LAND and ASP for per-input sample budgets and rollout scheduling; treat the TD paper as theory, not a deployment change.
